Hazleton Area Garden Club meeting: 6 p.m. Thursday, July 16. Hazle Township Commons Building, West 27th Street, Hazle Township. Program by Sandy Visintainer, member and master gardener, who will share her expertise on growing roses. Design, Traditional Mass Design “The Earth Laughs in Flowers.” Page 71 of 2017 Flower Show Handbook. Plant Material-Designer’s Choice. Horticulture I, Fresh flowers from the garden. Horticulture II, Anything special. Club member Chris Leskosky will present the workshop. The design will be Pot-et-Fleur. Public is welcome.
Third Annual Rockin’ the Mountain Music Series: Area open 3 p.m.; show starts 4 p.m. Saturdays, July 18 and 25. City View Park, Hazleton. All welcome; all ages; free. Food trucks, beer tent. Outside food and adult beverage not allowed. Bring folding chairs or a picnic blanket. July 18, BonPoison with opening act Tori V and the Karma; July 25, A Proud Monkey tribute to Dave Matthews Band with opening act Triple Fret.
Hazleton Power and Harwood Fire Company hosts Bangs, Bags and Bucks Bingo: Doors open 4 p.m.; games start 5:30 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Twenty total games, including five specials. Thousands of dollars in prizes, tricky trays, 50/50 raffle, homemade food, a bake sale and alcoholic drinks. Advance tickets only, $50; includes one card to play every game and one entry into the door prize. For tickets and information, visit Hazletonpower.org.
Anthracite Model Railroad Society hosts Annual Christmas in July open house: Noon to 4 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, July 18-19 and 25-26. Society headquarters, 1056 Hanover Court, Hazle Township. Thomas the Tank Engine will be bringing some of his friends to operate on the model Railroad on July 18-19; this weekend geared for younger engineers. Celebrate Christmas in July on July 25 with a special holiday theme. Admission free; donations appreciated.
Wyoming Trail Council of Pennsylvania’s Native Americans hosts The Return to Gnadenhutten Intertribal Native American Festival and PowWow: 10 a.m. to end Saturday, July 18; 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday, July 19. The Hofford Mill grounds, 500 Bridge St, Weissport. Grand entry at noon both days. Many tribes will represent their style of ancient and modern dance while wearing beautiful regalia associated with the various dances and tribal customs. Native American vendors with handcrafts, blankets, furs, jewelry, knives and art, a tricky tray tent. Proceeds benefit The Wyoming Trail Council. Bring a lawn chair or blanket. For information or to make donations, contact Robin Summerbird Hoffman at 570-436-2390 or Bonnie Becker at 484-892-0148. Donations can also be mailed to WSM at 292 Buck Mountain Road, Weatherly, PA 18255. Make checks payable to WSM.
Swing for Sight Golf Tournament: Registration, 10 a.m. Friday, July 24. Sands Springs Country Club. Cost, $100. Tricky trays open to the public from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.; Winners don’t need to be present for drawing. Supports The Community Services For Sight.
Hazleton Area Garden Club sponsors “Tea and Talk with the Author”: Two sessions, 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. or 2:30 to 4:30 p.m. Saturday, July 25. Sophia Coxe Estate House, Route 940, Drifton. Features Pamela Hubbard of Effort, author of “The Contemporary Cottage Garden”, who will speak and sign her book. Cost, $40; includes beverages, light luncheon, and a book. Reservations very limited due to space requirements. To RSVP or for information, call Chris at 570-606-5917.
Hazleton Art League hosts Red, White and YOU! group exhibition: Through Sunday, July 26. Hayden Family Center for the Arts, 31 W. Broad St., Hazleton. Features artists from throughout the Greater Hazleton area. Each work explores a unique aspect of the American experience, reflecting themes of history, community, heritage, innovation, and civic life. Also on display will be Legacies for Success: Luzerne County Women of Impact, a collection of period-style clothing presented by Dress for Success Luzerne County, honoring influential women from the region’s history. For information, call 570-455-3333, visit hazletonartleague.org, or stop by the center.
Hazleton Art League presents two-day workshop by Master Portrait Artist Gavin Glakas: Saturday, Aug. 8 and Sunday, Aug. 9. Hayden Family Center for the Arts, 31 W. Broad St., Hazleton. Designed for artists ages 18 and older, the workshop will feature a live model and is open to participants working in any medium. The event is the second in a series of special workshops organized by Hazleton Art League board member and instructor Jane Butkovsky. Glakas is an acclaimed portrait painter whose work is included in the permanent collections of the U.S. Congress, the Virginia State Capitol, the Central Intelligence Agency, universities, museums, and numerous public and private collections. He teaches at Georgetown University School of Medicine and conducts workshops throughout the United States and internationally. Registration, $350. Space is limited. To register or for information, call the Hazleton Art League at 570-455-3333 or visit hazletonartleague.org.
Anthracite Region Antique Automobile Club of America Anthracite Region of the Antique Automobile Club of America 40th annual Car Show: 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 20. Tri-County Little League Field, 600 Hancock St., McAdoo. Rain or shine. Special Participation Award to the first 150 registered vehicles; Special Awards to Best of Show Stock and Best of Show Modified. Dash plaques to the first 200 registered vehicles (pre-registration until Sept. 11). Special Awards to all AACA Senior and First Junior automobiles (must be registered by Sept. 6). No judging show. Gates open at 8 a.m.; day of show registration until noon; awards at 2:30 p.m. All antiques, classics, street rods, rat rods, modifieds, trucks, customs, motorcycles, and muscle cars welcome. Tri-County Little League will have food and beverages available. Live music by the Legends Oldies Band. For information and registration forms, visit http://www.araaca.com.
Grier City Sunday School yard sale: 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. Friday, July 31 and Saturday, Aug. 1. School, 202 Grier Ave, Barnesville. Treasures, bake sale, food sale, household, holiday, clothing of all types, women’s up to size 4X, shoes and more. Rain or shine. For information, call 570-467-2443.
Butler Township senior citizens general meeting: 1 p.m. Thursday, July 16. Community center. Annual indoor picnic. Hot dog and barbecue provided; all members are asked to bring a cover dish. New members welcome. For information, call Gale at 570-788-5606.
Butler Township senior citizens general meeting: 1 p.m. Thursday, Aug. 13. Community center. Bingo games. New members welcome. For information, call Gale at 570-788-5606.
Drums Duplicate Bridge Club meetings: Every Monday from late morning to early afternoon. For information, call Drew at 570-590-1249.
Conyngham Valley Historical Society sponsors summer concert: 6 p.m. Sunday, July 19 (rain date, July 26). Borough building, 215 Main St., Conyngham. Featuring husband-wife duo The Two of Us performing a wide variety of music from golden oldies to more modern tunes. Free; open to the public. Bring a chair or blanket.
Soup For Lunch hosts Patriotic Picnic: Noon, Tuesday, July 21. Conyngham United Methodist Church. Picnic-style luncheon. Enjoy good food, friendly conversation, and hometown fellowship. Cost, $5. RSVP to Beverly at 570-956-6793.
Conyngham Crime Watch hosts National Night Out: 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Tuesday, July 28. Whispering Willows Park, Main Street, Conyngham. Food trucks, ice cream, tricky trays, music, kids’ corner, and grilled hotdogs, hamburgers and fries. Meet and greet first responders including EMS, fire, police, troopers along with their equipment; State Rep. Jamie Walsh; tables with representatives providing helpful information.
The 40th Annual C.H.H.I.P.S. Trot-N-Brew: 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. Saturday, Aug. 15. Conyngham. A 1.5 mile novelty race through the streets. Competito
